name: Guillaume de la Descorde
vampire_desc: Second son of a marcher lord who built power through feuds and shifting alliances

marks.description: Guillaume's left eye no longer reflects light correctly. The iris has faded into a pale grey-white with a faint metallic sheen, as though frost permanently coats the surface beneath the pupil. In darkness, the eye catches candlelight too sharply, producing a dull predatory glimmer that unsettles anyone who notices it for too long.
marks.concealment: Guillaume hides the eye through layered social habits rather than disguise alone: he positions himself in low or indirect light, avoids prolonged eye contact, keeps his hair slightly longer on the left side, and occasionally wears a dark reading lens or narrow riding hood while traveling. Most effectively, he learned to weaponize aristocratic restraint: people interpret his distant gaze as nobility, exhaustion, or age rather than supernatural corruption. Those who do notice the eye often leave the encounter remembering not the defect itself, but the unsettling feeling that Guillaume saw more in them than they intended to reveal.

experiences: Born in 1182 to a minor marcher lord near a disputed frontier. Inherited little land but an instinct for division. Built power through feuds, shifting alliances, marriages, debts, and whispered promises. By middle age, became indispensable to greater lords who publicly condemned him while privately relying upon. A negotiator of truces that never fully hold, patron of mercenaries, and master of exploiting quarrels between neighboring houses. Chroniclers described him with admiration and unease in the same sentence.

He resolved a disputed claim over the Toll Bridge of Saint-Vire by using Feudal Ledgercraft and sealing a revised interpretation with the Signet of Descorde, causing both rival lords to withdraw without battle; He felt quietly detached satisfaction, less like a victor in a conflict and more like an administrator correcting an inevitable error in the order of things.

During a harsh winter, Guillaume uses Border Friction Engineering alongside the intelligence archive of the Black Chest of Vaucelles to deliberately sustain a controlled dispute between two neighboring lords over grain routes, ensuring neither can dominate the other while secretly redirecting surplus supplies through his own toll network; the effort leaves him feeling calmly pragmatic, as if stability is something that must occasionally be manufactured from imbalance.

When a well-connected noble begins pressing claims over a lucrative river toll, Guillaume uses Feudal Ledgercraft and a personal document from the Black Chest of Vaucelles—a sealed monastic confession implicating the noble in a concealed act of kin-slaying—to ensure the dispute is withdrawn before it reaches royal judgment, converting what would have been a public contest into a quiet, private concession; he feels a cold, pragmatic control, he has won without ever needing to fight.

Believing he has uncovered a hidden network of falsified monastic records tied to the immortal Isolde de Vézin, Guillaume arrives at a secluded abbey crypt carrying documents from the Black Chest of Vaucelles, intending to use controlled blackmail as leverage over what he assumes is merely an unusually entrenched noble conspiracy; the negotiation collapses when he realizes too late that Isolde's influence spans generations because she herself has endured them, and after he attempts to threaten exposure, she answers not with panic but with predatory curiosity, feeding from him within the crypt before forcing her blood into him as judgment rather than mercy. He feels first disbelief, then humiliation, and finally a terrible clarity as his heartbeat slows and he understands that for the first time in his life he has encountered something that cannot be negotiated with because it exists entirely outside the systems he mastered.

resources.name: The Signet of Descorde
resources.description: Engraved with a fractured cord motif. Seals charters, toll grants, and private treaties. Any document bearing its seal is treated as legally plausible unless explicitly disproven in court.

resources.name: The Black Chest of Vaucelles
resources.description: An iron-bound oak chest in a monastic dependency, containing sealed charters, debt acknowledgments, and sworn confessions. It is Guillaume's strategic archive of leverage—partially shielded by ecclesiastical authority, making unauthorized access politically perilous.

resources.name: The Toll Bridge of Saint-Vire
resources.description: A fortified stone bridge spanning a contested river crossing. Equipped with gatehouses and barracks, it serves as an economic engine and a diplomatic pressure point by taxing commerce and selectively controlling regional mobility.

characters.name: Hugues de Saint-Rémy
characters.description: An aging castellan who took Guillaume in as a page. Taught him discipline, resourcefulness, and the value of peace.

characters.name: King Philippe II
characters.description: The Quiet Architect of Instability. King of France who uses indirect manipulation to maintain control. Uses Guillaume to keep rival barons from consolidating power.

characters.name: Brother Étienne de Vaucelles
characters.description: A papal legate sent to enforce reform. A dangerous figure for Guillaume, as his work turns ambiguous local politics into clear legal or church matters.

characters.name: Isolde de Vézin
characters.description: To the living world, once the widowed lady of a ruined estate swallowed by forest and plague during the late 8th century. Official records describe her as dead after a winter fever, but the monastery that buried her keeps a sealed crypt beneath its chapel foundations. She is not dead — merely hidden, enduring, and patient. A predator who spans generations, she has manipulated local property and monastic politics for centuries. Guillaume's attempt at blackmail brought her attention to him; her response was to feed from him and force her blood into him as judgment, not mercy.
